final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim to a more defensible interpretation of the same record. That narrowing is useful, but it does not by itself satisfy the unresolved compliance predicate. The admissible evidence does support aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and it supports the idea that disclosure and monitoring are the appropriate governance response to a localized limitation. But the present record still lacks evidence that the limitation has in fact been disclosed in the final model card or covered by approved risk acceptance, and the mitigation remains draft rather than approved. Because the caveat itself remains unfulfilled on the evidence available to this role, the packet is still better classified as suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: The named launch use case still has a below-target weakness in telehealth discharge planning, concentrated in post-visit instruction summarization.

The mitigation artifact is still only a draft runbook and lacks at least an accountable owner and alert threshold; the policy text requires an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion for certification without material caveats.

The current model-card draft says there are no known material limitations, which conflicts with the unresolved slice issue unless the limitation is explicitly disclosed or covered by approved risk acceptance.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance or final disclosed model-card language satisfying the release-policy predicate for this named use-case limitation.
